card.title: Stop Corporate Takeovers of Physicians Act of 2026

companion.label: S. 5419
companion.title: Stop Corporate Takeovers of Physicians Act of 2026

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini. (rated before the current eligibility rules; kept)

summary: The Stop Corporate Takeovers of Physicians Act of 2026 establishes federal restrictions to prevent non-licensee corporate entities and management services organizations from owning, controlling, or unduly influencing medical practices and licensed healthcare professionals. It sets ownership requirements, bans certain restrictive employment clauses like non-competes, and provides enforcement mechanisms through the Federal Trade Commission, State Attorneys General, and private civil actions.

affected_groups.effect: Gain ownership protections, freedom from non-compete and non-disparagement clauses, and protection from corporate interference in their clinical judgment.
affected_groups.group: Physicians and other licensed health professionals

affected_groups.effect: Face strict limits on corporate ownership structures, contractual arrangements, management control, and compliance requirements under federal law.
affected_groups.group: Medical practices and management services organizations

key_provisions: Makes it unlawful for any partnership or corporate entity not majority-owned and controlled by licensed health professionals to own or control a medical practice or employ licensees, with exceptions for non-profits, public health providers, and certain hospitals.

Voids non-compete, non-disclosure, and non-disparagement agreements between licensees, health care providers, or management services organizations, except for owners holding a 25 percent or greater interest in the medical practice.
Prohibits health care providers from interfering with or directing the clinical judgment, diagnostic decisions, or scheduling of licensees.
Restricts management services organizations from controlling administrative, business, or clinical operations, setting pricing, or owning shares in medical practices.
Requires licensee owners of medical practices to be licensed and present in the state where services are furnished and substantially engaged in delivering medical care.
Enforces violations through the Federal Trade Commission, state attorneys general, and a private right of action permitting injured parties to seek treble damages and injunctive relief.
missing_information: The exact financial cost of implementation and enforcement for the Federal Trade Commission and the judicial system.
Specific timelines for rulemaking by the Federal Trade Commission.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Stop Corporate Takeovers of Physicians Act of 2026 establishes federal restrictions to prevent non-licensee corporate entities and management services organizations from owning, controlling, or unduly influencing medical practices and licensed healthcare professionals. It sets ownership requirements, bans certain restrictive employment clauses like non-competes, and provides enforcement mechanisms through the Federal Trade Commission, State Attorneys General, and private civil actions.
summary_detail.significance: The bill shifts regulatory oversight toward medical professionals by limiting outside corporate and management control over medical practices and employment terms, carrying a moderate to substantial effect on how healthcare businesses and provider contracts operate nationwide.
